newsitem.title: USA: Missouri Gas granted rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Missouri Gas granted rate increase.

text.p: Southern Union Co said Thursday its Missouri natural gas distribution division, Missouri Gas Energy, was granted a $7.53 million annual rate increase, effective February 1.

The Missouri Public Service Commission order also recognized that "the Trust Originated Preferred Securities issued by Southern Union Financing Company I constitute the creation of equity, not debt," the company said.
Southern Union Chief Financial Officer Ron Endres said the company is encouraged the commission acknowledged compliance with the commission's capital structure requirement.

Endres also said "the rate increase will have a positive effect on the company's after-tax net cash flow of approximately $4.5 million annually, but is expected to have a minimal impact on future net earnings since previously deferred expenses are now recognized and offset with the annual increase to revenues."
Southern Union said the commission denied the company's request to increase the $9.05 monthly residential customer service charge to $15.00 per month; and set an 11.3 percent return on equity.
The commission also reduced the carrying cost rate applied on the spending incurred on Missouri Gas' natural gas safety program since early 1994, Southern Union said.

Pursuant to a 1989 commission order, it explained, Missouri Gas is engaged in a major safety program which includes the replacement of natural gas service and yard lines and cast iron and bare steel mains.

In connection with a related accounting authority order issued in 1994, the company was authorized to defer certain costs of this program including carrying costs that were ordered to be deferred at the specified rate of 10.54 percent.

The company said it does not believe that the portion of the rate case order reducing the carrying cost rate retroactively to 1994 is lawful. It will seek rehearing of at least that portion of the rate order, and if necessary, will pursue a court appeal on this matter.

Absent a reversal of this part of the rate case order, the company would have to record a one-time $6 million pre-tax write-off of the previously deferred costs. This write-off would be exclusive of the prospective effects of the $7.53 million annualized increase to revenues, Southern Union said.
